name: ARM NEON / Advanced SIMD (128-bit)
description: 128-bit SIMD on all AArch64 processors. TBL instruction provides flexible byte lookup; widening multiplies for packing. Processes 16 input bytes (12 output) per iteration.

key_instructions.purpose: 16-byte table lookup indexed by another vector. Core of base64 ASCII-to-value mapping. Single-register variant sufficient for 16-entry LUT.
64-byte table lookup (4 source registers). Can cover full Base64 alphabet (64 entries) in one logical operation.
key_instructions.note: Expensive on A76/N1 (4 CPI). Improved on N2. For base64, prefer nibble-decomposition with TBL-1 over TBL-4.

key_instructions.purpose: Unsigned widening multiply: 8B x 8B -> 8H. Used for multiply-based packing of 6-bit values.
Alternative to multiply-based packing. Shift and insert for bit-field merging.
Structure load/store with deinterleaving. LD4 loads 4 interleaved streams into 4 registers (useful for splitting 4-char groups). ST3 stores 3 registers interleaved.
key_instructions.note: LD4 can directly deinterleave base64 input into 4 separate register for parallel lookup.

base64_applicability: Available on ALL AArch64 hardware. NEON base64 approach from Mula's base64simd: (1) TBL-based nibble lookup (2 TBL-1 + comparisons, ~8 instructions), (2) multiply-based or shift-based packing (~4-6 instructions), (3) TBL for output rearrangement (1 instruction). Total ~14-16 instructions per 16 input bytes. Expected 3-4x over scalar. Key advantage: dual ASIMD pipes on A76/N1/N2 give 0.5 CPI for most instructions.
